newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank supervision to be scrutinised.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank supervision to be scrutinised.

text.p: Thailand has set up a new commission to scrutinise the Bank of Thailand's examination and supervision of the country's troubled financial institutions, a senior finance ministry official said.

The commission, set up on the recommendation of the World Bank, would focus on central bank failures in supervising troubled financial institutions that cost the government billions of baht, the official said late on Monday.
The commission would produce recommendations on how to reform the central bank's examination and supervision activities, he added.
Former finance minister Suthee Singhasaneh would head the body, the official said.
Thailand's debt-ridden financial sector has been hit by a severe liquidity crunch and overexposure to depressed property firms.
The central bank in June suspended 16 weak finance firms and ordered them to consolidate or merge with five stronger ones.
In the past, the central bank has examined and then used government funds to bail out some finance firms and banks, such as the debt-laden Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.

Some analysts believe the central bank may have failed in its supervisory role given the large number of troubles in the finance sector as Thailand goes through its worst economic downturn in over a decade.
